evidence.definition: Lower secondary school starting age is the age at which students would enter lower secondary education, assuming they had started at the official entrance age for the lowest level of education, had studied full-time throughout and had progressed through the system without repeating or skipping a grade.
evidence.source_organization: Data API, UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), uri: https://databrowser.uis.unesco.org/resources, note: The data are obtained through the UIS API.  Detailed documentation is available at: https://api.uis.unesco.org/api/public/documentation/, publisher: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS), date accessed: 2026-03-19, date published: 2026-02
evidence.universe: mapped countries and territories with data

claims.text: Places Ranked by Middle School Starting Age
claims.support: Indicator SE.SEC.AGES measures lower secondary school starting age across mapped countries and territories.

claims.text: MIDDLE SCHOOL AGE
claims.support: Indicator SE.SEC.AGES measures lower secondary school starting age.

claims.text: Children in Southern Africa typically enter lower secondary school four years later than those in Turkey or Ukraine.
claims.support: Namibia (NAM): 14 years, South Africa (ZAF): 14 years, Tanzania (TZA): 14 years, Zambia (ZMB): 14 years. Turkey (TUR): 10 years, Ukraine (UKR): 10 years. Difference is 4 years.

claims.text: In Turkey, children enter middle school at 10. In Namibia, they wait until 14.
claims.support: Turkey (TUR): 10 years, Namibia (NAM): 14 years.

claims.text: In Brazil and the UK, students make that transition at 11.
claims.support: Brazil (BRA): 11 years, United Kingdom (GBR): 11 years.

claims.text: This benchmark assumes students entered on time and progressed without repeating any grade.
claims.support: Definition: assuming they had started at the official entrance age for the lowest level of education, had studied full-time throughout and had progressed through the system without repeating or skipping a grade.

claims.text: Climbing the ladder, the USA, Japan, and China all begin at 12.
claims.support: United States (USA): 12 years, Japan (JPN): 12 years, China (CHN): 12 years.

claims.text: Moving higher, Denmark and Indonesia wait until students reach 13.
claims.support: Denmark (DNK): 13 years, Indonesia (IDN): 13 years.

claims.text: At the very top, Namibia has the world's highest starting age at 14.
claims.support: Namibia (NAM): 14 years, rank 1.

claims.text: At what age do students enter lower secondary school in your country?
claims.support: General closing question.
